Uomo di 57 anni. RX del torace in proiez: 57-year-old man. PA chest X-ray. The collection gives no symptoms or reason for the examination.
Valuta l'ombra cardiaca (puoi misurarla): Assess the cardiac silhouette (you can measure it) and conclude.
Ombra cardiaca ingrandita: rapporto card: Enlarged cardiac silhouette: cardiothoracic ratio above 0.5
Diametro trasverso massimo del cuore div: Maximum transverse diameter of the heart divided by the maximum internal diameter of the thorax, on the same PA image.
Campi polmonari senza versamento né edem: Lung fields without evident effusion or alveolar oedema
Sulla RX un cuore grande non distingue t: On X-ray a large heart does not distinguish chamber dilatation from pericardial effusion: echocardiography is needed.
Cardiomegalia: ecocardiogramma per capir: Cardiomegaly: echocardiography to find the cause (dilated chambers, hypertrophy, pericardial effusion)
Cuore normale: in PA l'ombra cardiaca è: Normal heart: on PA the cardiac silhouette is always overestimated
È la proiezione AP (letto, paziente sedu: It is the AP projection (bedside, patient sitting) that magnifies the heart; on PA a ratio > 0.5 is significant.
Il rapporto cardio-toracico (RCT) si mis: The cardiothoracic ratio (CTR) is measured only on a well-inspired PA: maximum transverse diameter of the heart (from the midline to the right border plus to the left border) divided by the maximum internal diameter of the thorax. Above 0.5 is cardiomegaly. On AP, in expiration or with the patient supine the heart looks larger and the value is not reliable. The X-ray cannot distinguish dilated chambers, hypertrophy and pericardial effusion: that is why echocardiography is done. Also look for signs of heart failure: vascular redistribution, Kerley B lines, effusions.
RCT > 0,5 solo in PA ben inspirata; poi: CTR > 0.5 only on a well-inspired PA; then look for signs of heart failure.
Riquadro della lesione disegnato dai rad: Box drawn around the lesion by the NIH radiologists (BBox_List_2017: «Cardiomegaly»). No clinical data, histology or follow-up.
